bib.title: On the Effect of Dropping Layers of Pre-trained Transformer Models
bib.venue: Journal of Computer Speech and Language (preprint submitted August 16, 2022)

read.skipped: Reference list after offset 45014 skimmed only for lineage.

question: Is the whole network of a pre-trained transformer needed for downstream GLUE tasks, and which layers can be dropped before fine-tuning with least loss?
hypothesis: Top layers are specialised to the pre-training objective and neighbouring layers are redundant, so some layers can be dropped with little loss; lower layers are most critical.
contributions: Six layer-dropping strategies (top, bottom, alternate, symmetric, parameter-based, contribution-based) applied to BERT, RoBERTa, ALBERT, XLNet and DistilBERT on GLUE
Dropping top layers works consistently, giving 40% size reduction while keeping up to 98.2% of performance
Pruned models are on par with knowledge-distilled models without retraining a new model
Distilled models and ALBERT can also be pruned
Models differ in learning dynamics: RoBERTa and XLNet learn task knowledge earlier than BERT

method.summary: Drop K encoder layers from a pre-trained 12-layer model by one of six strategies, then fine-tune on a GLUE task for three epochs and evaluate on the official dev set. Compare strategies, tasks, models, and distilled baselines.
method.task: Layer pruning of pre-trained transformers for GLUE classification and regression

datasets.name: SST-2
datasets.split: official dev set used for reporting (test sets not public)

training.objective: task-specific fine-tuning with a task layer added on the last retained layer

other.defaults: transformers library default settings, parameters not optimised
other.gradual_dropping: drop one layer after every two epochs of fine-tuning; no improvement
other.excluded_tasks: WNLI (irregular dataset) and CoLA (large variance) left out
other.K_values: K = 2, 4, 6 for 12-layer models; K = 1, 2, 3 for DistilBERT

inference.samples: single fine-tuning run per configuration is implied; no seeds reported

parameters.contribution_threshold: cosine similarity of CLS before/after layer averaged over dev set; thresholds 0.95, 0.925, 0.9 (chosen empirically)
parameters.inference_timing: QQP dev set, 40.4k instances, batch size 32
parameters.task_specific_depth: dev set split into equal hold-out and dev halves; minimum layers kept within 1%, 2%, 3% loss

metrics.name: GLUE dev score
metrics.definition: task metric on official dev sets as reported (accuracy-style; STS-B regression); averages over tasks used in figures

metrics.name: Fine-tuning speedup
metrics.definition: times faster than the original network

baselines: Vanilla-KD, BERT-PKD, BERT-TH (from Xu et al.)
GLP6 greedy layer pruning (Peer et al.)
eval.protocol: McNemar test at p=0.05 on RTE difference; 5-task subset (SST-2, MNLI, QNLI, QQP, STS-B) for discussion section; default settings, no hyperparameter search

evidence.quote: task-specific fine-tuning using GLUE training sets for three epochs

results.claim: Dropping the top 6 of 12 layers cuts BERT/RoBERTa parameters by about 40% and speeds fine-tuning and inference by about 50% with 0.89-2.91 points average loss.
results.setup: GLUE, top-layer dropping K=6, BERT/RoBERTa/XLNet base, 3 epochs fine-tuning

results.claim: Top-6 dropping parameter counts and speedups: BERT 110M to 66M, fine-tuning 1.94x, inference 50% lower.
results.setup: BERT base, K=6, inference time on QQP dev 40.4k instances batch 32
results.table: Table 3, row 6/12, columns Param. 66M, Fine-tuning 1.94, Inference 50%

results.claim: RoBERTa with top 2 layers dropped scores at or above the full model on several tasks (e.g. SST-2 93.46 vs 92.20).
results.setup: RoBERTa base, top-2 dropped, dev set

results.claim: QQP on XLNet stays within 1% of the full model with 9 of 12 layers dropped, a 60% parameter and 80% inference-time reduction.
results.setup: XLNet, QQP, task-specific optimal depth, top-layer dropping
results.quote: This corresponds to 60% reduction in the number of parameters and 80% reduction in terms of inference time.
results.note: Table 4 XLNet QQP at 1% threshold: 9 layers, 0.60 hold-out loss

results.claim: Top-6 dropping loses only 2.91 (BERT) and 1.81 (XLNet) points on average and beats other strategies at K=6; bottom dropping is worst.
results.quote: with an average loss of only 2.91 and 1.81 points for BERT and XLNet

results.claim: A distilled model (DistilBERT) can be pruned by a third with 0.75 points average loss.
results.quote: pruned by a third, with an average loss of 0.75 points only

results.claim: Pruned BERT-6 and RoBERTa-6 are competitive with KD-distilled 6-layer models, e.g. RoBERTa-6 QQP 90.91 vs DistilRoBERTa 89.40, without training a new model.
results.setup: Top-6 dropped RoBERTa vs DistilRoBERTa; baselines taken from other papers
results.table: Table 6, row 10 RoBERTa-6 column QQP vs row 9 DistilRoBERTa
results.note: BERT-6 trails on MNLI/QNLI/SST-2 vs DistilBERT? BERT-6 MNLI 81.13 vs DistilBERT 81.78

results.claim: QQP and STS-B are least affected by layer dropping; RTE/MRPC swings are statistically insignificant (McNemar, p=0.05) because dev sets are small.
results.quote: a loss of 0.72 only for BERT

results.claim: RoBERTa and XLNet performance matures near layer 7, while BERT improves up to layer 11.
results.quote: the performance matures close to the 7th layer of the model while BERT improves with every higher layer until the 11th layer

results.claim: ALBERT with top 6 layers dropped keeps performance (SST-2 90.14, above full 89.79) though parameters are shared so memory is not saved.
results.quote: 6-layered model is 90.14, which is 0.35 points absolute better than the baseline

results.claim: Dropping layers after fine-tuning then re-fine-tuning is comparable to dropping from the pre-trained model; gradual dropping gave no gain.
results.note: BERT-6 SST-2 is 92.25 in Table 7 but 90.25 in Table 2 (same configuration)

limits: Base-size models only; BERT-large and XLNet-large not run for memory (TitanX 12GB).
Default hyperparameters, no tuning; optimiser, lr, batch size, seeds not reported; apparently single runs.
GLUE classification only; CoLA and WNLI excluded; dev sets used for reporting, and small RTE/MRPC dev sets are noisy.
Parameter- and contribution-based strategies are task-agnostic; task-specific variants left to future work. Contribution-based worked poorly on BERT.
Dropping layers is static: unlike dynamic early exit, all inputs use the same reduced depth.
ALBERT saves speed but not memory because of parameter sharing.
Distillation and LayerDrop comparison numbers are copied from other papers, with possibly different settings.

terms.definition: drop top K layers; output of layer L-K serves as last layer, and a task-specific layer is added on top
contribution of a layer is cosine similarity between its input and output CLS representations; layers above a threshold are dropped
retain top and bottom X layers, drop K middle layers where 2X+K=L
